kicker: The teacher of Hafsa رضي الله عنها
title: Ash-Shifa’ bint Abdullah
Ash-Shifa’ means “the {{gold}}healer{{/gold}}”
body: It was her nickname — her real name was Layla. Medicine was her work, in Makkah even before Islam, and later in Madinah.

title: She turned her house into a {{gold}}clinic{{/gold}}
body: Anyone who needed medicine would go to Ash-Shifa’, and she would help them.

title: She taught Hafsa to {{gold}}read & write{{/gold}}
body: When few could read, she taught Hafsa رضي الله عنها, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, writing and calligraphy.

title: Umar gave her {{gold}}authority{{/gold}} over the market
body: Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه entrusted her with the market’s business and financial affairs.

title: A home the Prophet ﷺ {{gold}}visited{{/gold}}
body: She kept a blanket and an izar for him — her children inherited them. Her son became a reciter of the Qur’an, her grandson a narrator of hadith.

title: “A female companion we could never imagine how great she was.”
